sections.title: A Rainy Afternoon
sections.content: Rain rearranges a day, so this is the vocabulary of the indoor version: a café nearby, something hot to drink, cards and stories until it stops. Three ordinary verbs come with it — ver, creer and caer. 'Ver' is irregular only in the yo form, 'veo', and 'creer' behaves like 'leer' from Lesson 6.

items.spanish: Desde la ventana veo la lluvia caer sobre las calles.
items.english: From the window I watch the rain falling on the streets.

items.spanish: Creo que hoy no hacemos el pícnic.
items.english: I don't think we're having the picnic today.

items.spanish: Carlos pide chocolate caliente para todos.
items.english: Carlos orders hot chocolate for everyone.

items.spanish: La lluvia es perfecta para leer un libro.
items.english: Rain is perfect for reading a book.

sections.content: 'La carta' is both a playing card and a letter — and, on a restaurant table, the menu. Context does the work, as it does with 'el plato'.

sections.topic: vocabulary for the seasons and the weather
